---
title: "Does the model's geometry agree with what AeroSandbox computes from it?"
---

{{< include _model.qmd >}}

Every reference quantity the chapter uses, computed a second time from the
traced tables and set against what `AeroSandbox` reports from the assembled
geometry. Two of them disagreed, and both disagreements were the model being
wrong rather than the library.

```{python}
wing, stab, fin = mceagle.wings

# The independent arm: integrate the traced chord tables directly, the way the
# model used to. eta runs along the panel, so these are flat-pattern values --
# the foam you cut.
traced = {
    "wing area [cm²]":    2 * np.trapezoid(wing_c, wing_eta * b_w / 2) * 1e4,
    "stab area [cm²]":    2 * np.trapezoid(stab_c, stab_eta * b_h / 2) * 1e4,
    "fin area [cm²]":     np.trapezoid(fin_c, fin_eta * b_v) * 1e4,
    "wing span [mm]":     b_w * 1e3,
    "wing aspect ratio":  b_w ** 2 / (2 * np.trapezoid(wing_c, wing_eta * b_w / 2)),
    "mean geo chord [mm]": 2 * np.trapezoid(wing_c, wing_eta * b_w / 2) / b_w * 1e3,
}
library = {
    "wing area [cm²]":    wing.area() * 1e4,
    "stab area [cm²]":    stab.area() * 1e4,
    "fin area [cm²]":     fin.area() * 1e4,
    "wing span [mm]":     wing.span() * 1e3,
    "wing aspect ratio":  wing.aspect_ratio(),
    "mean geo chord [mm]": wing.mean_geometric_chord() * 1e3,
}
worst = max(abs(library[k] / traced[k] - 1) for k in traced)
```

**Answer.** Yes now, and it did not before. The two disagreements were both real
defects.

The wing was built from flat-pattern chords placed at *projected* span stations,
so `Wing.span()` reported `{python} f"{b_w/np.cosd(dihedral)*1e3:.1f}"` mm for a
wing meant to span `{python} f"{b_w*1e3:.0f}"` mm — the model needed a
30.8 cm flat pattern to build a 30 cm glider. Sections now sit at arc length
along the panel, so the flat pattern is the 300 mm the plan is scaled to and the
finished glider measures `{python} f"{b_proj*1e3:.1f}"` mm across. `Wing.area()`
and the traced integral now agree to
`{python} f"{worst*100:.4f}"`% (@tbl-crosscheck).

The second was `c_ref`. Static margin is quoted throughout this chapter as
"% MAC", but the denominator was the mean *geometric* chord,
`{python} f"{wing.mean_geometric_chord()*1e3:.2f}"` mm, not the mean
aerodynamic chord, `{python} f"{wing.mean_aerodynamic_chord()*1e3:.2f}"` mm —
`{python} f"{(wing.mean_aerodynamic_chord()/wing.mean_geometric_chord()-1)*100:.1f}"`%
apart. `c_ref` is now the MAC.

The neutral point does not move under that change, and that is worth stating
because it is the check that the change was safe rather than merely plausible:
`x_np = x_ref − (dCm/dCL)·c_ref`, and `Cm` scales as `1/c_ref`, so the product is
invariant. It reads `{python} f"{neutral_point()*1e3:.1f}"` mm before and after.
What does change is what "10% MAC" *means*: the target CG moves from
`{python} f"{0.10*wing.mean_geometric_chord()*1e3:.2f}"` to
`{python} f"{0.10*c_w*1e3:.2f}"` mm ahead of the neutral point, so the ballast
for a given static margin rises
`{python} f"{(c_w/wing.mean_geometric_chord()-1)*100:.1f}"`%.

The stabilizer is the one row that still disagrees, by
`{python} f"{(stab.area()/(2*np.trapezoid(stab_c, stab_eta*b_h/2))-1)*100:.2f}"`%.
That one is not a defect: `area()` lofts the surface including its
`{python} f"{i_h:.0f}"`° twist, while the traced integral is the flat pattern it
is cut from. It is an eighth of the tracing uncertainty already stated, and mass
is charged on the flat pattern.

```{python}
#| label: tbl-crosscheck
#| tbl-cap: "Each reference quantity computed twice — integrated from the traced chord tables, and read off the assembled geometry. Agreement is the point; the stabilizer's residual is its twist."
import pandas as pd

pd.DataFrame({
    "quantity": list(traced),
    "from the traced tables": [f"{traced[k]:.3f}" for k in traced],
    "from the geometry": [f"{library[k]:.3f}" for k in traced],
    "difference [%]": [f"{(library[k]/traced[k] - 1)*100:+.3f}" for k in traced],
}).style.hide(axis="index")
```
